newsitem.title: USA: Radisys plunges on fraud allegations.
newsitem.headline: Radisys plunges on fraud allegations.

text.p: Radisys Corp shares plunged 19 percent after a former vice president sued the semiconductor company alleging that executives misrepresented financial results.
Shares of Radisys, based in Beaverton, Ore., fell 7-1/4 to 43-3/4 in late morning trading. Earlier, the shares traded as low as 41-1/2.

In a lawsuit filed in Oregon's Washington County Circuit Court, Bruce Taylor, former vice president of operations, alleged that he uncovered "significant discrepency in the financial records of Radisys" involving the reporting of the company's inventory and other matters. The company misrepresented the numbers both before and following its Oct 1995 public stock offering, the suit alleged.
Taylor, who could not be immediately reached for comment, also alleged he was dismissed immediately after he raised the issue with the company's executives, the lawsuit said.
Officials of Radisys, which makes computer chips for telecommunication and medical devices, could not immediately be reached for comment.
Financial magazine Barron's first reported the lawsuit in today's issue.
